notes.text: Upon me — Though the prophet may speak of himself, yet it is principally to be understood of Christ. Anointed - Set me apart, both capacitating him with gifts, and commissioning him with authority; and yet more, as it is applied to Christ, a power to make all effectual, from whence he hath also the name of Messiah among the Hebrew, and of Christ among the Greeks; nay, Christ alone among the prophets hath obtained this name, Psalm xlv, 7. The prophet describes first, who Christ is, and then what are his offices. Liberty - This appertains to Christ's kingly office, whereby he proclaims liberty from the dominion of sin, and from the fear of hell.

Vengeance — It being necessary, that where God will deliver his people, he should take vengeance on their enemies; principally on the enemies of his church, and the spiritual ones chiefly, Satan, sin, and death.

Ashes — By ashes understand whatever is proper for days of mourning, as by beauty whatever may become times of rejoicing. Oil of joy - He calls it oil of joy in allusion to those anointings they were wont to use in times of joy, gladness for heaviness; and it is called a garment in allusion to their festival ornaments, for they had garments appropriated to their conditions, some suitable to times of rejoicing, and some to times of mourning. Called - That they may be so. Trees - That they shall be firm, solid, and well rooted, being by faith engrafted into Christ, and bringing forth fruit suitable to the soil wherein they are planted.

glossa.text:
*The Spirit of the Lord* ((HIER.)) Christ according to the humanity, who had said above, *I the Lord, in the time will gather them,* etc.

*Because he hath anointed me:* with the oil of gladness, with the abundance of grace. ((ID.)) This anointing was completed in the baptism, because the Spirit of the Lord descended in the likeness of a dove, and remained upon him.

*To announce.* The Seventy: To preach the Gospel to the poor.

*An opening,* namely a loosing; for thus Symmachus more openly rendered it.
*The day of vengeance:* ((ID.)) of damnation, which came through the Romans, according to that: *The day shall come,* etc. And, *when you shall see Jerusalem compassed about with an army,* etc.

*A crown.* When, that is, they shall have seen that very many of the Jews have believed, and that they receive a most clean robe for a mourning garment.

*For ashes.* For the grief and sorrow of their own fruits, when, that is, they shall have seen the Gentiles flowing together to the faith, they shall have the oil of joy for mourning, the mantle of praise for the spirit of grief.

notes.text: Turned — Brought the captive Israelites out of Babylon into their own land. Dream - We were so surprized and astonished.

Turn — As thou hast brought us home, bring also the rest of our brethren. As - As thou art pleased sometimes to send floods of water into dry and barren grounds, such as the southern parts of Canaan were. We must trust in God for success in all enterprizes, ver. 1, 2. And for children, ver. 3-5. A song of degrees of Solomon.

glossa.text: *A canticle of degrees.* ((CASS.)) The seventh degree, in a figure of the Old Testament, prophesies through Christ who is to come the return from captivity, as it were from Babylon: whence now consolation, and a sowing that more may be reaped. ((AUG.)) Those redeemed by the blood of Christ and turned back from captivity sing these things, while they are pilgrims, groaning by the way. Sion is Jerusalem, eternal in the angels, captive in men. *In the turning.* ((CASS.)) First the greatness of the deed is shown, with the greatness of the joy: secondly he prays for the turning from captivity still to come, there, *Turn again, O Lord. In the turning.* ((AUG.)) Or, when he shall have turned, etc., *as far as turn again, O Lord, our captivity. As.* ((ID.)) It is not always set for a likeness, but for a property, as here; whence it is also said: He did as a just man, which he truly is; so these are made *as men comforted,* that is, they rejoiced, as receiving consolation in the resurrection of Christ, who went before that we might follow.

*Our mouth.* ((CASS.)) The secret of the heart, where joys first are, which afterwards break forth by the office of the tongue. ((AUG.)) *Our mouth.* Of the heart: thence proceeds the evil and the good which cleanses or defiles us; whence not: *That which proceedeth out of the mouth, defileth ((Marc. VII))* . Not of the mouth of the flesh, but of the heart. For thou art not unclean if thou namest thefts and other evils: but while thou thinkest of them, even if thou keep silence. *Among the Gentiles.* ((ID.)) Not the Gentiles, because not all believe. *He hath magnified,* because they see them work miracles also; a firm testimony from an adversary. ((CASS.)) And he has truly magnified, lest thou doubt because of the words of the Gentiles.

*Turn again, O Lord.* ((ID.)) The second part. He prays for the turning which is to come, in which there shall be a sowing in hope of joy. ((ID.)) The redemption of the coming of the Lord having been foretold, they pray again that their own sins be forgiven. In the general remission they rejoice, and they pray pardon for themselves. *Turn again, O Lord, our captivity.* ((ID.)) There was none according to the letter in the days of David, but under the devil the world was captive, etc., *as far as* it is not therefore to be given over, because *he that soweth in tears.* ((THEOD.)) He calls Jerusalem the south, etc., *as far as* that they may be constrained, and make their way after the manner of a torrent.

*In tears.* ((AUG.)) Spiritual sowing is always in tears, whence: *Blessed are they that mourn.* But they who sow in the flesh, sow with gladness: but afterwards weeping: because *mourning taketh hold of the end of joy.* ((ID.)) Zacchaeus, *Behold the half,* etc., *as far as: He that shall give a cup of cold water shall not lose his reward ((Matth. X))*.

*Going.* ((CASS.)) By the advancement of a better life. *Casting,* sending on before them into that world. *Their own,* not of rapine, but of their own labour; *coming,* to the judgment. This is common to all, but to joy none come but the good. *And they wept.* ((AUG.)) Because they were wretched, etc., *as far as* he wishes that many be sick.

notes.text: Rejoice evermore — In uninterrupted happiness in God. Pray without ceasing - Which is the fruit of always rejoicing in the Lord. In everything give thanks - Which is the fruit of both the former. This is Christian perfection. Further than this we cannot go; and we need not stop short of it. Our Lord has purchased joy, as well as righteousness, for us. It is the very design of the gospel that, being saved from guilt, we should be happy in the love of Christ. Prayer may be said to be the breath of our spiritual life. He that lives cannot possibly cease breathing. So much as we really enjoy of the presence of God, so much prayer and praise do we offer up without ceasing; else our rejoicing is but delusion. Thanksgiving is inseparable from true prayer: it is almost essentially connected with it. He that always prays is ever giving praise, whether in ease or pain, both for prosperity and for the greatest adversity. He blesses God for all things, looks on them as coming from him, and receives them only for his sake; not choosing nor refusing, liking nor disliking, anything, but only as it is agreeable or disagreeable to his perfect will.
For this — That you should thus rejoice, pray, give thanks. Is the will of God - Always good, always pointing at our salvation.

Quench not the Spirit — Wherever it is, it burns; it flames in holy love, in joy, prayer, thanksgiving. O quench it not, damp it not in yourself or others, either by neglecting to do good, or by doing evil!

Despise not prophesyings — That is, preaching; for the apostle is not here speaking of extraordinary gifts. It seems, one means of grace is put for all; and whoever despises any of these, under whatever pretense, will surely (though perhaps gradually and almost insensibly) quench the Spirit.

Meantime, prove all things — Which any preacher recommends. (He speaks of practice, not of doctrines.) Try every advice by the touchstone of scripture, and hold fast that which is good - Zealously, resolutely, diligently practice it, in spite of all opposition.

And be equally zealous and careful to abstain from all appearance of evil — Observe, those who "heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears," under pretense of proving all things, have no countenance or excuse from this scripture.

And may the God of peace sanctify you — By the peace he works in you, which is a great means of sanctification. Wholly - The word signifies wholly and perfectly; every part and all that concerns you; all that is of or about you. And may the whole of you, the spirit and the soul and the body - Just before he said you; now he denominates them from their spiritual state. The spirit - Gal. vi, 8; wishing that it may be preserved whole and entire: then from their natural state, the soul and the body; (for these two make up the whole nature of man, Matt. x, 28;) wishing it may be preserved blameless till the coming of Christ. To explain this a little further: of the three here mentioned, only the two last are the natural constituent parts of man. The first is adventitious, and the supernatural gift of God, to be found in Christians only. That man cannot possibly consist of three parts, appears hence: The soul is either matter or not matter: there is no medium. But if it is matter, it is part of the body: if not matter, it coincides with the Spirit.
Who also will do it — Unless you quench the Spirit.

glossa.text: *In Christ.* The will of God has been shown, because these things were in Christ, in whom nothing displeased God. *Extinguish not the Spirit.* Because it is the will of God to do all these things, you who are greater, who have through the Holy Spirit the gift of understanding, hide it not, by which desert you also would lose it. You subjects, despise not their prophecies; nevertheless receive not all things indiscriminately, but *prove* them, that is, examine them by reason, and hold what is found good. *Extinguish not the Spirit,* that is: If the Holy Spirit reveals anything to anyone's ear, forbid thou him not to speak what he perceives. The Holy Spirit who has been given to us we extinguish, not as to what is in himself, but in us, when by sinning we put him to flight.

*And may the God of peace himself sanctify you in all things,* etc. That is, I thus admonish prelates and subjects, but God himself is he who is able. *Your spirit.* Let the reason be kept entire, by not consenting to the flesh. *And soul.* That is, let the sensuality be kept entire, by serving the reason. *And body.* That you do nothing by its ministry. Whence anyone may complain. Sometimes the soul is defiled by an evil thought and yet the body is clean. And therefore he says that the spirit ought to be entire in man. But if an evil life, or an evil thought, intervene, there will not be spirit. Spirit and soul and body, of which man consists, namely that by which we understand, and that by which we live, and that by which we are visible and palpable, which again are called two, because often the soul is named together with the spirit. *Without complaint.* It is one thing to be without sin, which in this life was said of the Only-begotten alone. It is another to be without complaint, which could be said of many just men even in this life. For there is a certain manner of good life, of which even in this present conversation there could be no just complaint. *In the coming.* That is, even unto the end of life.

*Faithful.* As if he should say: I pray that he may sanctify, that he may keep you sanctified; nor is there to be any doubt thereof, because he is true in his promises, who called you to this, that you should be holy.

notes.text: There was a man — The evangelist now proceeds to him who testified of the light, which he had spoken of in the five preceding verses.

The same came for (that is, in order to give) a testimony — The evangelist, with the most strong and tender affection, interweaves his own testimony with that of John, by noble digressions, wherein he explains the office of the Baptist; partly premises and partly subjoins a further explication to his short sentences. What St. Matthew, Mark, and Luke term the Gospel, in respect of the promise going before, St. John usually terms the testimony, intimating the certain knowledge of the relator; to testify of the light - Of Christ.

glossa.text: *There was a man sent.* After he had ascended by a lofty flight beyond every nature into the height of theology, because he had contemplated that the Word had always been with the Father, he presently descends to the lowliness of human nature, and particularly of the Word's forerunner, against those who said that human nature had been in the first parent wholly lost and brought to nothing. *A man sent.* A man, not an angel, as the heretics will have it, sent from God. Therefore he was able to speak of God.

The Lord has done great things for us
I will give you as a light to the nations

doctrine.title: Nicene Creed
doctrine.article: the Holy Spirit, the giver of life

registers.label: Spare
lines: The Spirit of the Lord is upon us.
Good news for the poor, release for the captive.
Those who went out weeping, carrying seed—
come home with shouts of joy.
A man came, sent from God, to point to the light.
We are not the light; we testify to it.
Come, let us worship with mouths full of laughter.
Come, Lord Jesus. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: When the Lord turned our captivity, we were like those who dream — our mouths filled with laughter, our tongues with shouts of joy.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
He has clothed us with the garment of praise, traded ashes for a garland, mourning for the oil of gladness.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
So we who went out weeping, carrying our small handful of seed, come home with our arms full of sheaves.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Rejoice always; the One who calls you is faithful. Come, point to the light with us.
Come, Lord Jesus, come. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The Spirit anoints us with the oil of gladness.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Ashes are traded for a garland of joy.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
We sow in tears and come home singing.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Come, let us worship and point to the light.
Come, Lord Jesus, come. Amen.
